CORRECTION to this bead's completion note. I claimed "SharedKernel is already dead — modules/core/.../SharedKernel.scala has ZERO references anywhere in the repo, so item 3 is satisfied in substance." That was WRONG, and the error was in my method, not just the conclusion.

I grepped for the identifier "SharedKernel" and found nothing. But the file declares PACKAGE-LEVEL aliases in io.github.bbuchsbaum.slurm4s.core:

    type SubmissionKey = io.github.bbuchsbaum.remoteexec.kernel.SubmissionKey
    val SubmissionKey = io.github.bbuchsbaum.remoteexec.kernel.SubmissionKey
    ... and ~20 more

Nothing names "SharedKernel" precisely BECAUSE the aliases are package-level: every `import io.github.bbuchsbaum.slurm4s.core.*` resolves SubmissionKey, ValidationFailure, OperationId and the rest through this file. Grepping for the filename identifier was the wrong probe entirely.

Measured, not assumed: deleting the file produces 610 compile errors in core alone. Restored, and the tree compiles clean.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS BEAD: item 3 (remove the compatibility aliases) is NOT done. What IS done is removing the worker AtomicFiles facade, which genuinely had no consumers outside its own test. The ADR 0010 alias surface remains, and removing it is a real migration rather than a deletion: every consumer that currently gets these names via `core.*` must import io.github.bbuchsbaum.remoteexec.kernel explicitly. ADR 0010 anticipates exactly this — "these pre-1.0 aliases carry no independent semantics and may be removed after downstream migration" — and the migration has not happened.

That work should be its own bead, sequenced before P7.6 cuts the compatibility baseline, since it changes the public import surface of slurm4s-core.

The other three D6 items (ssh->agent cut, ssh->worker cut, kernel purity) stand as reported and are verified.
